findings.evidence: Identical argument blocks at InvariantMass.lean:130-132, 142-144, 154-156, 165-167, 255-257; the `rw [... ] at this` line at 145, 157, 258 (and `at hc`).
findings.fix: Add two lemmas in the `CollinearPhoton` section — `(q + P).spatialPart = (a - p) • n` and `(q + P).timeComponent = k + E` — and use them in all five proofs. Both are physically meaningful (total momentum and total energy of the photon–target system) and are currently reusable facts buried in proof bodies.
findings.issue: The derivation of the system's spatial part `(q+P).spatialPart = (a-p) • n` and its time component `|a - p| < (q+P).timeComponent` is rebuilt inline in five proofs — lines 130-133, 142-145, 154-157, 165-167, 255-258 — each repeating `spatialPart_add_eq_sub_smul_of_spatialPart_eq_smul hq' hP'` plus `(by rwa [timeComponent_add_eq_add_of_timeComponent_eq hq hP])`, with `rw [timeComponent_add_eq_add_of_timeComponent_eq hq hP] at this` repeated four more times.

findings.evidence: `have hpar := inner_spatialPart_eq_of_spatialPart_eq_smul hn hv` / `have h' : ... := by rwa [hpar]` appears identically at Rapidity.lean:176-177, 187-188, 199-200.
findings.fix: Extract a lemma, e.g. `abs_inner_spatialPart_lt_timeComponent_of_spatialPart_eq_smul (hn : ‖n‖ = 1) (hv : v.spatialPart = a • n) (h : |a| < v.timeComponent) : |⟪v.spatialPart, n⟫_ℝ| < v.timeComponent`, and call it in the three `_of_spatialPart_eq_smul` proofs.
findings.issue: The conversion of the collinear light-cone hypothesis `|a| < v.timeComponent` into `|⟪v.spatialPart, n⟫_ℝ| < v.timeComponent` is repeated verbatim in three proofs (lines 176-177, 187-188, 199-200), and the `rwa [← minkowskiProduct_self_eq_sq_sub_inner_sq_of_spatialPart_eq_smul hn hv, hpar] at this` step twice (190, 202).

summary: Proofs are otherwise robust (linear_combination over rewrite chains, no change/show, documented defeq use), but the same two-to-three-line hypothesis derivation is repeated verbatim in five proofs in InvariantMass.lean and three in Rapidity.lean, hiding facts that should be named lemmas.
